summary: Premise: the Galois-orbit equation Tr_{K/Q}(1/x) = 4/p (x ∈ O_K totally positive, K cyclic cubic) is a variant, not a reformulation of ES over Z (x ∈ Z would give 3/x = 4/p); writing Tr(1/x) = s2(x)/N(x) it is p·s2(x) = 4N(x), and for p INERT in K this forces x = p·y with Tr(1/y) = 4, i.e. it is p-independent: solvable for all inert p iff some totally positive z ∈ O_K has Tr(1/z) ∈ 4ℤ_{>0} (PROVED, elementary; x = p(Tr(1/z)/4)z). Search (conductors 7, 9, 13, 19, box |coords| ≤ 60, ~4·10⁵ totally positive x each; also 31, 43, 73 box 40): every prime p ≤ 10⁴ solved is split in K (cond. 7: all split p ≤ 139 hit, no inert or ramified p ever), and NO totally positive z has 4 | Tr(1/z) (integral Tr(1/z) occurs 51–187 times per field with residues 1, 2, 3 mod 4), while without positivity 4 | Tr(1/z) is common (258 cases, cond. 7, box 25) and in non-cyclic totally real cubics m = Tr(1/z) ≡ 0 (4) is abundant (34 768 polys for m = 4, a ≤ 120) but cyclic (square disc) has 0 for m = 4, 8, 12, 16 vs 2–31 for every other m ≤ 16 (EVIDENCE). CONJECTURE: a positivity-dependent, cyclic-specific obstruction 4 ∤ Tr(1/z) (in fact Tr(z)·Tr(1/z) ≢ 0 (mod 4) in all 75 cyclic hits) blocks every inert prime; PROVED for units when 2 is inert and totally positive units are squares (F₈ trace argument: Tr(w̄) = Tr(w̄⁻¹) = 0 impossible).
not_done: No proof of the mod-4 obstruction for non-units (2-adic discriminant analysis shows it is not a 2-adic condition on D alone: D ≡ 1 mod 8 is possible; Hilbert-symbol/trace-form route not completed); split primes beyond the box (p > ~300) not solved, so 'all split p solvable' is untested beyond ~139; only Z[θ] (index 2/3 orders) for conductors 31, 43, 73.
next: Try to prove 4 ∤ Tr(1/z) for totally positive z in cyclic cubic fields via am − 9 = Tr((z−σz)²/(zσz)) (u totally positive, N(u) = (Δ/c)²) or a Hasse-invariant computation of Tr(y v²); it would be a clean positivity+reciprocity obstruction of the type ES lacks (Bright–Loughran).

summary: Premise checked: for 4/n = 1/x+1/y+1/z, χ^orb(S²(x,y,z)) = −1 + 4/n, area 2π(1 − 4/n), hyperbolic iff n ≥ 5. Elliptic terms written and checked: in the Selberg trace formula for Δ(x,y,z) each cone point of order m contributes Σ_{k=1}^{m−1} (4m sin(πk/m))⁻¹ ∫ h(r) cosh((π − 2πk/m)r)/cosh(πr) dr (|centraliser| = 2m in SL₂; normalisation fixed numerically), whose heat-kernel limit is (m² − 1)/(12m), matching the exact spectrum of the football S²/Z_m (m = 1, 2, 3, 5, to 10⁻⁹); hence a₀ = Area/4π = (1 − 4/n)/2 and a₁ = −(1 − 4/n)/6 + Σ(x_i² − 1)/(12x_i). So 'area = 2π(1 − 4/n)' is spectrally characterised only by Weyl's law (a restatement), and by Doyle–Rossetti (arXiv:1103.4372, abstract verified: the spectrum determines and is determined by area, number of cone points of each order and geodesic data) distinct ES triples are never isospectral, i.e. #ES triples of n = #triangle-orbifold spectra with Weyl constant (1 − 4/n)/2; a₁ alone does not separate them (1 663 equal-(a₀, a₁) pairs among the 50 595 triples with 5 ≤ n ≤ 300, first (4,8,8)/(5,5,10) at n = 8; none at prime n ≤ 300). Assessment: the trace formula is an identity for a given group and offers no mechanism producing a triangle group of prescribed area — no ES content.

summary: Verified Heath-Brown, Acta Arith. 72 (1995) 235–275, Thm 1 (read in the original PDF): Σ*_{m≤M}|Σ*_{n≤N} a_n (n/m)|² ≪_ε (MN)^ε(M+N)Σ*|a_n|², where m and n run over odd squarefree integers and a_n is INDEPENDENT of m (Cor 1–3 cover all real primitive characters and non-squarefree n). ES side (derivation from BM_CORRECTED_COUNT §1–2, Thm 1.1(3), Prop 2.1(d,e)): R(p) = M_BM(p) + X_BM(p), where X_BM collects every character mod q=4uB except 1 and χ_{−4uB}. In X_BM the modulus is q and the argument is the single point p, so at fixed p there is no mean square for HB to act on: HB with one modulus is plain Cauchy–Schwarz, and the non-real characters, which carry the lower-tail problem, lie outside HB altogether. The item's own form (modulus 4C, argument d | 4Cp+1) breaks HB's hypothesis that a_d does not depend on the modulus; this is exactly the tied-modulus B2 coupling. The only place where HB's roles fit is the BM term T(p) = Σ_{m≤p/4, 2|m} (−m/p)2^{ω(m)}/(4φ(m)), with modulus p averaged over primes and argument m. There the loss can be stated exactly (scripts/z52d_p2_ZF1_Z1448_hb.py, 300 primes ≡ 1 (4) after P0 = 10⁴, 10⁵, 10⁶): the true mean T² is 2.09, 2.95, 3.60, while the HB shape gives (1+N/M)Σ|a|² = 1.41–1.43 times (MN)^ε·log M (EVIDENCE). So HB is sharp up to P^ε but averaged only (B6), and it is superseded by the PROVED pointwise T(p) = (σ/4)E·L(1,χ_p)² + O(p^{−1/16}log p) (BM_LVALUE Thm A); Elliott's ε-free form (6) is useless here, with shape ~10³–10⁶.

summary: Premise is FALSE as stated: no Hooley (or other) GRH theorem for x²+y²+z³ was found. Jagy–Kaplansky, Exp. Math. 4 (1995) 169–173 (abstract read) record that all integers are x²+y²+z³ with mixed signs, that the all-positive problem is open with computations suggesting finitely many exceptions, and that x²+y²+z⁹ has infinitely many. The real Hooley GRH theorem is n = p + u² + v² (Acta Math. 97 (1957) 189–210; Thm 1 read, p. 209). On ERH the count is (πn/log n)·∏(1+χ₄(ℓ)/(ℓ(ℓ−1)))·∏_{ℓ|n}(explicit factor), and the singular series is bounded below for every n (no local obstruction; main term ≫ n/(log n log log n)). The method is Σ_p r(n−p) = 4Σ_d χ₄(d)π(n;n,d), a Titchmarsh divisor problem with a FIXED character χ₄, GRH on average over d ≲ √n, and a Brun-sieve treatment of the sign changes for the remaining d. Comparison with ES local densities (derivation from FRONTIER §2.1–2.2): the ES fibre over C is the hyperbola (4uC−1)(4BC−1) = 4Cn+1, whose count D⁻_{4C}(4Cn+1) = φ(4C)⁻¹Σ_{χ mod 4C}χ(−1)σ_χ(N) involves all characters to a modulus that moves with the fibre (Hooley: one fixed χ₄ per fibre). Its local factor M_BM is 0 or 2/φ(4uB) per pair and vanishes identically at odd squares, with total size ≍ log²p (Hooley: ≍ n/log n, i.e. M1a). Hooley's averaged variable is the prime p, independent of the modulus d; in ES the only long variable u (or C) sits inside the class modulus 4u — exactly the tied-modulus obstruction (FRONTIER §3, Remark 3.1). So neither the GRH input nor the sieve transfers.

Then D = −dp² is not fixed (|D| ≍ x² for the natural range c ≤ p/4d, while the constants are ≪_D), and above all the class modulus 4cd moves with the summation variable c, so 1[f ≡ −p (4cd)] is neither λ(q) nor a_m b_n — the tied-modulus B2 event. summary: Verified Polymath8a (ANT 8 (2014), arXiv:1402.0811) Def. 2.6(iii)/Thm 2.8. Type III[ϖ,δ,σ] bounds Σ_{q≤x^{1/2+2ϖ}, q x^δ-densely divisible}|Δ(α*ψ₁*ψ₂*ψ₃; a (q))| ≪ x log^{−A}x for SMOOTH ψ_i at scales x^{2σ} ≤ N_i ≤ x^{1/2−σ} and one coherent residue a, i.e. τ₃-type convolutions to level > 1/2. ES side (derivation from ET arXiv:1107.1010 §5): f_II(n) is not a τ₃ convolution in n. With n + 4a²d = e(4acd−1), f_II(n) = Σ_{a,d} #{m | n+4a²d : m ≡ −1 (4ad)}, a sum over shifts of class-restricted τ₂ (Titchmarsh-divisor shape). Restricted to n ≡ b (mod q) it is the same with moduli lcm(4acd−1, q). ET's lower bound Σ_{p≤N}f_II(p) ≫ N log²N uses Bombieri–Vinogradov only at level N^{0.3} (a,c,d ≤ N^{0.1}, read p. 21–22). summary: I wrote the forest constraints χ(u)=χ(v) for all edges uv | p+u+v with u<v≤V (including u=1 with χ(1)=1) as an F₂ system on x_q=[χ(q)=−1] over the primes q≤V, and computed which χ(q)=1 are forced. With V=1000 and 30 random primes p≡1 (4) per scale 10⁶…10²⁰ there are ≈40 edges, rank ≈23 and ≈21 forced primes of 168 (always the small ones: e.g. χ(2)=1 via edge (1,2); χ(3)=1 via (1,3) or (2,3)). The implied bound D(χ,1;p^{1/4})² ≤ 2Σ_{unforced q} 1/q has mean 0.18 (10⁶), 0.52 (10⁸), 0.90 (10¹⁰), 1.10 (10¹²; min 0.90), and ≥1.15 + 2log(log X/log V) beyond. The comparison is the standard Burgess+Vinogradov bound D(χ_p,1;p^{1/4+ε})² ≥ 1−o(1) (if Σ_{χ(q)=−1,q≤x}1/q < ½−δ then Σ_{n≤x}χ(n) ≥ 2δx). That bound is asymptotic, while the edge bound grows like 2 log log X − O(log log log X), because only O(log²V) primes are ever constrained, so no contradiction arises for large p. Moreover each forced χ_p(q)=1 is a congruence condition on p ('p is a square mod q', recovering Mordell's square classes), i.e. B1; this matches BRAINSTORM/bsB_sterile_pretentious.md §Dictionary 2 (hard p ⇔ χ_p pretends to be 1) without adding a forcing mechanism.
not_done: Edges with an endpoint > 1000 (which involve large primes) were not included; no Halász-type quantitative upper bound for the hypothetical χ was derived; no correlation study between the true D(χ_p,1;X) and N₋(p) (the BM_LVALUE T(p) ~ L(1,χ_p)² analysis already covers that main-term link).

summary: Realisability made exact: face areas are A_i = 3V/h_i, and four positive numbers are the face areas of a non-degenerate tetrahedron iff each is < the sum of the other three (Minkowski: close a non-planar 4-gon of area-weighted unit normals). Scaling then fixes the altitudes, so '4/n = Σ_{i≤4} 1/h_i realisable' ⇔ every h_i > n/2 (PROVED, elementary), exactly as for triangles (sides ∝ 1/h_i). The tetrahedral version is therefore trivially solvable for every n by the regular tetrahedron h_i = n. Even with DISTINCT integer altitudes it holds for every 5 ≤ n ≤ 20 000 (fails only at n = 3, 4, where the sum of four distinct admissible unit fractions is too small; exhaustive C search, EVIDENCE). By contrast the realisable triangle (3-term) version fails at all 211 primes p ≡ 1 (4) ≤ 3000 (and at 74 other n), reproducing the repo's proof (Z1931, scripts/z52b_translate_cheap.py). So the 'dimension ladder' degenerates at d = 3: realisability bites only in the plane, where it kills ES at every prime p ≡ 1 (4).
not_done: No proof of the distinct-altitude version for all n (only n ≤ 20 000); higher simplices (d ≥ 4) and integrality of other data (edges, volume, Heronian-type conditions) not considered.

summary: The natural quadric is already in the repo: words ↔ γ_w = [[A,n],[t,A*]] = (HJ product M(u)M(t)M(v) up to signs) on AA* − tn = 1 (signature (2,2); its SO(2,1)/adjoint image gives the (2,1) form), QUESTION_R.md Prop 1.1, which notes the gap 'these sets are not semigroup orbits'. I did the missing orbit test. PROVED (elementary): if g ∈ SL₂(ℤ) satisfies gW₃ ⊆ W₃ (W₃ = all length-3 word matrices), then g = T^k, k ≥ 0. Proof: for g = [[α,β],[γ,δ]] with γ ≠ 0, letting u → ∞ at fixed t, a′+1 = t(αu+β)−α+1 ≡ 0 mod c′ = t(γu+δ)−γ forces α = kγ and t(β−kδ)+1 = 0, impossible for t ≥ 2. CERTIFIED: among all 116² pairs (g,h) ∈ SL₂(ℤ)² with entries ≤ 3, tested on the 343 words with t,u,v ≤ 8, exactly the 32 pairs ±(T^a, T^b), 0 ≤ a,b ≤ 3, satisfy gW₃h ⊆ W₃ (these are u ↦ u+a, v ↦ v+b). So W₃ = ⊔_t T^ℕ γ_{(t,2,2)} T^ℕ is a union of parabolic (abelian, non-Zariski-dense) double orbits, one per level t, and no thin Zariski-dense group acts on the ES₅ word data in this quadric; an Apollonian/HKRS-type orbit would need a different encoding, and none was found.
